assessments.reasoning: The HTTPS page at data.norge.no/nlod/en/2.0 declares English HTML and names the Norwegian Digitalisation Agency as author. Its title and §§2 and 10 identify the 2.0 data licence. The captured SHA-256 equals the claim revision 8c9abba2b7498f057e3f78bcf4a41d9c7328b12e5bd08ff85b274d18cc0d0862.

The License row in the Index’s docs/SCOPE.md at cdff8aeed68bf1f9c62d8c86159c7dc08b2d75d7 admits a grant or licence with identifiable text and edition supported by a controlling source. Its opening paragraph includes relevant data. The Agency’s edition-specific text and §2 grant satisfy that criterion. Actual selection is a separate Index decision.

limitations: Active is the intended Index lifecycle mapping. Current admission, application to a particular work, redistribution rights and installation eligibility require separate records.
The identity covers the pinned English publisher representation. Norwegian-language identity and compatibility are outside scope.
reasoning: The Agency’s English HTML identifies “Norwegian Licence for Open Government Data (NLOD) 2.0”. Its §10 reservation explicitly names version 2.0, and §2 grants conditional permission to copy, distribute, modify and combine information. Under SCES-1.0 §§1–3, the captured publisher revision supplies authority for this exact edition, while the Index’s scope document governs the proposed license classification.
